Today the Epic initialization creates an agent that writes PRDs sometiems, then the PRDs get executed from independent sessions. What would be the change to get these session to subsession more close to eachother without violating the Scheduler role of metering sub-sessions effeceively

**Current state (confirmed in code):** Epic session (architect) mints its own `claudeSessionId` via `--session-id`/`--resume` (chatRunner.cjs:533-537). PRD jobs are deliberately isolated — `scheduler.cjs` spawns `claude -p` with a **fresh** `--session-id` (scheduler.cjs:2240/2590), and PRD_AUTHORING.md explicitly documents this as intentional: "the PRD body MUST be self-contained — `claude -p` runs it on a fresh Sonnet session with NO conversation context" (scheduler.cjs:2399).

**Key finding:** the Scheduler's metering role (`sessionSlots.cjs`) is a pure process-count gate — "may one more `claude -p` launch right now?" — completely agnostic to whose session identity is being resumed. It doesn't care if a job is `--session-id <fresh>` or `--resume <existing>`. So changing session lineage for PRD jobs doesn't touch metering at all; those are genuinely orthogonal today.

**Two directions, given that:**

- **A — literal shared session** (`--resume <epicSessionId>` for PRD jobs): real continuity, but forces PRDs of one Epic to run serially (can't `--resume` the same session id concurrently), needs a new mutual-exclusion lock against the Epic's own interactive Chat/Terminal attachment (extends the existing "mutually exclusive view attachment" invariant to a third consumer), and pollutes one transcript with both architect discussion and dev-lead tool-call noise — undermining the "self-contained PRD, judged on its own AC" design that PRD_AUTHORING.md's stuck-job postmortems (fizzpop, etch-engine) actually lean on.

- **B — richer linkage, same isolation** (recommended): keep PRD jobs on fresh, independent, parallelizable sessions, but stop treating the PRD file as the *only* thing dev-lead sees. Derive a condensed context digest from the Epic session's transcript (same AIM-framework spirit as `composeEpicIntake`/`summarizeGroundingBoard`) and prepend it to the PRD's opening prompt, and record provenance (`sourceSessionId`/turn-range) on the PRD so it's inspectable. ## Schema consistency

**No runtime schema exists for the `PromptSession` record itself, at any layer.**

- `PromptSession` (`src/renderer/state/promptSessions.ts:29-76`) is a TS-only interface — compile-time, erased at runtime. Data read back from disk is `as`-cast, not parsed.
- The IPC boundary (`ipcSchemas.cjs:217-248`, `promptSessionsMergeActiveIndex`) validates the **envelope** only — id charset/length, map size caps, prototype-pollution guard — but each session value is `z.unknown()`. `status`'s 3-value union, `tag`'s enum, `createdAt` format: none of it is checked on the wire.
- Worse: **two independent code paths hand-construct the same record.** The renderer's New Epic flow (`promptSessions.ts:352-379`, `createPromptSession`) builds a `PromptSession` object literal directly and never touches `ensureEpic`. The CLI/scheduler path (`epicMint.cjs:216-351`, `ensureEpic`) builds a *different* object literal, with its own id scheme (`psess-<ts>-<seq>` vs `<slug>-<uuid8>`). They're kept in sync today by a doc comment ("stay shape-compatible so `hydrate()` reading a main-written index round-trips it") — convention, not enforcement.
- `ensureEpic` does enforce one real invariant well: the born-`proposed` law is fail-closed (throws if a mint call passes any status but `proposed`, `epicMint.cjs:299-305`) — so *lifecycle* is actually protected. It's field *shape* that isn't.
- Schema evolution so far = "make the new field optional and tolerate its absence" (`durableTurns`, `promptSessions.ts:85-91`) — never a real migration pass. `prdMigration.cjs` is a precedent for what a real one would look like; nothing equivalent exists for Epic records.

**Net risk:** a future field added to one constructor and not the other silently drifts — no test, no schema, no IPC check would catch it. It'd surface as a blank UI cell or a `hydrate()` crash on read, not at write time.

## Does the current workflow support dynamic assembly? Not really — for `home` specifically, no.

I checked the actual selection pipeline (`select.ts`'s `scoreVariants` + `selectionPredicates.ts`), not just the library structure.

**How selection actually works:** `scoreVariants` walks a lens's presets in order (v1, v2, …) and picks the first preset whose per-slot choice is "eligible." A variant is only *conditionally* eligible if it has an entry in `VARIANT_REQUIREMENTS` (`selectionPredicates.ts`) — a `requires`/`avoidIf` predicate checked against the project's real `ProjectPageSummary`. **If a variant has no entry there, it's unconditionally eligible, which means preset `v1`'s pick always wins the tie-break, on every run, for every project.**

**`VARIANT_REQUIREMENTS` has exactly two entries in the whole codebase, both in `marketing`:**
```
'marketing.proof.quote': { requires: ['quotes.length > 0'] }
'marketing.proof.stats': { requires: ['stats.length > 0'] }
```

Nothing else — not `home.overview`, not `home.pillars`, not anything in `feature` or `architecture` — has a predicate. So:

- **`home` lens (the one you're asking about): `overview` always resolves to `dashboard`, `pillars` always resolves to `grid` — for every project, every regenerate.** The `ledger`/`rows` alternates exist in the library but the deterministic selector can never reach them; they're only reachable if a human hand-edits `picks.json` directly (which `mergePicks` then preserves).
- Same is true for `feature` (always `v1`'s picks) and `architecture` (always `v1`'s picks) — `marketing` is the *only* lens with any real content-driven variation, and even there only 2 of its 8 slots actually branch.

So today, "assembled dynamically" is true only in the mechanical sense (there's a selection *pass*, and hand-picks are respected across regenerates) — it is not true in the sense that layout responds to what's actually in the project. A tiny CL…

## Confirmed: your 4-piece model replaces the current 5-stage pipeline

| Your term | Maps to (unchanged) |
|---|---|
| **The Project** | `project-pages/summary.json` (Stage 1 — agent reads brief.json + repo, writes summary) |
| **The Component Library** | `src/renderer/lib/projectPages/library/*.tsx` (Stage 0 — fixed slots/variants, still the only building blocks; the agent picks *among* these, doesn't invent new markup) |
| **Home Builder Agent** | `project-home-builder` (Epic tag + `.claude/agents/project-home-builder.md`) — now owns selection too, not just summary+render |
| **Place to host output** | `project-pages/picks.json` + `output/*.html` + `manifest.json` (Stage 3, unchanged) |

**What's actually being cut is Stage 2 only** — the deterministic, non-LLM `scoreVariants` scorer and its `requires`/`avoidIf` predicate language. That's exactly the piece I flagged last turn as producing a fixed layout (`home` always gets `dashboard`+`grid`, `feature`/`architecture` always get `v1`, because almost nothing has a predicate). Removing it and having the agent choose directly — reading the library's variant notes + `summary.json` itself, the same way it already writes `summary.json` — is the fix: variant fit becomes real per-project judgment instead of "whichever preset comes first in a list that's usually untriggered anyway."

Stage 3 (render) stays a deterministic pure function (`renderProjectPages(summary, picks)`) — that part was never the problem, it's just template instantiation from whatever `picks.json` says.

Two different things are getting conflated here — let me separate them.

**The "4" that already exists (unaffected by 957/958):** `project-home-builder`'s Stage 3/4 already pre-generates 4 static HTML pages per "Generate Now"/"Regenerate" click — `home`, `marketing`, `feature`, `architecture` (confirmed in `render.tsx:96`: `renderProjectPages` returns `{ home, marketing, feature, architecture }`, all written to `project-pages/output/*.html` in one pass). `ProjectPagesSection.tsx` displays them behind a lens-toggle. **But these 4 are not "4 target-audience versions of the same Home page."** They're 4 different *content types*, not 4 audiences viewing one page:
- `home` — an internal dashboard view (for someone who already has the project open)
- `marketing` — an outward pitch (the one genuinely audience-facing lens)
- `feature` — a single feature deep-dive
- `architecture` — an engineering/review-oriented page

Only `home` itself has 2 slots (`overview`, `pillars`), each with 2 layout variants — that's a style choice within one page, not 4 audience cuts.

**What 957/958 actually change:** today, the `home` lens's variant picks (`overview: dashboard`, `pillars: grid`) are hardcoded — every project gets the identical layout because the old deterministic scorer had no real predicate for them. Once those PRDs land, the `project-home-builder` agent picks those variants itself per project, so the *style* of the generated Home page will actually reflect the project instead of being frozen. That inventory doc covers app-chrome/localStorage scoping, not the `settings.json`↔Agent/Tag question — it's a separate, still-relevant open list. No overlap to reconcile.

**The rule, established and written into `CLAUDE.md` (session-manager-operations/../CLAUDE.md, new bullet after the AIM-framework paragraph):**

- **Settings (System/Project/Local) is substrate, not per-Epic curation.** It edits the actual `settings.json`/`.claude/` files the `claude` CLI reads from disk on every invocation, identically, regardless of which Epic is running. It was never really "one session" scoped — the old TAB=session model just hid this because a tab's one session and its one project settings.json had the same lifetime. Now that a TAB hosts many Epics, a Project-scope Settings edit changes the substrate for *every* Epic in that project (User-scope: every Epic machine-wide). There's no per-Epic override, and `groundingBoard.ts` only reports these files exist — it never injects their content into a prompt.
- **Agent + Tag is the per-Epic curation layer.** `agentType` (Actor) and `tag` (Mission) are folded fresh into each Epic's `openingPrompt` at creation via `composeEpicIntake` — that's the only place "how this specific Epic should work" belongs.
- **The rule to apply going forward:** if a behavior should differ per Epic or per task, it's a new/edited **Tag** (`TagLibrary.tsx`'s `initialPromptTemplate`) or a new/edited **Agent** persona (`AgentLibrary.tsx`'s persona `.md`, which literally is a system-prompt body) — never a Settings edit. Settings only holds what's legitimately identical for that scope regardless of task (permissions, hooks, MCP servers, env vars, default model, output style).

Verified via direct read of `Settings.tsx`, `scopes.ts`, `epicIntake.ts`, `groundingBoard.ts`, and confirmed by a parallel research agent — no code drift exists (Settings.tsx was already correctly file-scoped, never per-Epic); this was purely an undocumented mental-model gap, now closed wi…

`Model & Reasoning` (`src/renderer/lib/settingsGroups.ts:48-60`) is a curated grouping over six literal top-level `settings.json` keys: `model`, `availableModels`, `modelOverrides`, `effortLevel`, `fastMode`, `fastModePerSessionOptIn`, `alwaysThinkingEnabled`. It's not app logic — Settings.tsx just renders/edits these keys via the same ScopeSwitcher (user/project/local) as everything else in the JSON editor; the `claude` CLI itself reads them from whichever settings.json it loads.

So it falls under exactly the rule just written into `CLAUDE.md`: it's **substrate, not per-Epic curation**.

- Editing it at **User scope** (`~/.claude/settings.json`) sets the default model/effort/fast-mode for every `claude` process this machine launches — every Epic, every project, forever, until changed again.
- Editing it at **Project scope** (`<cwd>/.claude/settings.json`) overrides that for every Epic under this one project.
- There is **no per-Epic model/effort override** — an Epic doesn't carry its own `effortLevel`; it inherits whatever the substrate says at the moment its `claude --resume`/`claude -p` process spawns. Two Epics in the same project today literally cannot run on different models via this screen — only by hand-editing Local scope between them, which is exactly the kind of session-scoped mental model you're trying to retire.

Given the rule you just had me write ("if a behavior should differ per Epic/task, it's a Tag or Agent, never a Settings edit"), Model & Reasoning is a case where that rule currently has **no escape hatch** — Tag and Agent personas are *prompt text*, they cannot select a model or effort level (that's a `claude` CLI process-launch parameter, not something injectable into `openingPrompt`). So right now:

- If you want "this Epic always runs on Opus at high effort" as a *repeatable, curated* choice, the only real lever is Project/Local-scope `settings.json` — which is global to the project, not the Epic — or a `--model`/effort flag baked into how …

**Decision locked in and queued.**

Confirmed the mechanism exists but is inert: `AgentPersona` already carries a `model` frontmatter field (`src/main/agentLibrary.cjs`), and `chatRunner.cjs` already proves `--model` is a real, working CLI flag (it hardcodes `--model sonnet` today) — but nothing currently reads the persona's `model` at Epic-launch time. `agentType` is genuinely display-only right now, exactly as the current CLAUDE.md says.

Queued a 3-PRD chain on this Epic (`psess-msckxplj-24`) to close that gap:

- **959 `agent-model-default-terminal`** — Agent persona's `model` field becomes the `--model` flag on the Terminal-view `claude` launch command for that one Epic.
- **960 `agent-model-default-chat`** (depends on 959) — same resolution reused so chatRunner's headless Chat-view run agrees with Terminal (extracted into a shared resolver, `sonnet` fallback kept explicit per your global "pin `--model`" rule).
- **961 `agent-model-docs-and-scope`** (depends on 960) — corrects CLAUDE.md's now-stale "agentType is display-only" line and adds the carve-out to the Settings-substrate rule I wrote earlier this Epic.

Deliberately scoped to **`model` only**, not "all session settings": `effortLevel`/`fastMode`/`alwaysThinkingEnabled` (the rest of Settings' "Model & Reasoning" group) have no confirmed `claude` CLI flag anywhere in this codebase today — inventing one would be a guess, not a fact. PRD 961 documents that as an explicit known gap rather than letting the docs overclaim. If you want effort-level control added too, that needs the CLI mechanism confirmed first (worth a quick check against `claude --help` / the claude-api reference) — say the word and I'll queue a follow-up PRD once that's verified.

Queued **962 `agent-model-nav-consolidation`**, chained after 961 (dependsOn), completing the 4-PRD sequence for this Epic:

959 → 960 → 961 → 962: wire the model resolver (Terminal) → wire it (Chat) → correct the docs → relocate the UI so Agent Library owns curated model editing and Settings narrows to non-Agent substrate.

**Net answer to your question:** keep Settings as its own left-nav tab — it's not redundant, it's the home for everything that's legitimately machine/project-wide (permissions, hooks, MCP servers, git behavior, interface, memory/plans, updates) regardless of which Agent is running. Only the "Model & Reasoning" slice moves into Agent Library, because that's the one slice that's actually per-Agent now. Tags never get a settings surface, per your instruction — nothing in this chain gives them one.

**Queued 963 `nav-consolidate-home-scoped-config`**, completing a 5-PRD chain (959→960→961→962→963) for this Epic:

959/960 wire Agent persona `model` into an Epic's actual launch (Terminal + Chat) → 961 corrects the docs → 962 moves the "Model & Reasoning" editing UI into Agent Library → 963 pulls System Prompt / Skills / MCP Servers / Hooks / Permissions / Settings off the Project face's left-nav entirely, leaving them Home-only — matching the precedent already set by Plugins/Keybindings/Agent Library/Tag Library, and validated against `lib/navFace.ts`'s documented split between `navFace` and `activeTabId` (Project-scope editing still works from Home, since scope resolution depends on the active tab's `cwd`, not which face you're viewing).

`memory` and `bilko-host` deliberately stay on the Project face — they aren't `settings.json`-scope editors (workspace memory store, and a project-specific publish action), so they don't belong in this consolidation.

End state after all 5 land: Project face's left-nav holds only per-project/per-Epic things (Project Home, Epics, File Explorer, Scheduler, History, Memory, Host on Bilko.run); every machine/project-substrate config tab lives under Home, with zero duplication.

**Rule affirmed and closed with PRD 964.** Chain is now 6 deep (959→960→961→962→963, plus 964 branching off 959):

- **959/960** — Agent persona's `model` field becomes the real default for an Epic's launch (Terminal + Chat).
- **961** — docs correction.
- **962** — *editing* the model default moves into Agent Library (a catalog/definition, not session state — correctly stays off EPICS).
- **963** — substrate config tabs (System Prompt/Skills/MCP/Hooks/Permissions/Settings) consolidate onto Home only, out of the Project face.
- **964** (new) — *reading* which Agent/model a specific Epic is actually running with moves into EpicDetail — closing the gap you just flagged: nothing session-specific should require leaving EPICS to see.

The distinction locked in: **catalogs (Agent Library, Tag Library) define reusable defaults and belong in Home; EPICS is where a specific session's resolved state — which agent, which model, which tag — must be readable.** Editing always happens in the catalog; the Epic only ever displays a read-only readout of what it resolved to, since an Epic's agent/tag are fixed for its session lifetime per the existing lifecycle rule.

No other Home/Project nav item currently leaks session-specific state — Memory (workspace-wide) and History (cross-session aggregate) aren't single-Epic state, so they're unaffected.
